item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 172330
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM HST Mon Aug 17 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located a few hundred miles south-southeast of French
Frigate Shoals, Hawaii.

Western Portion of the East Pacific:
A broad area of low pressure is expected to form well to the
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands during the latter part of
this week. Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression could form
towards the end of the week or over the weekend while the system
moves generally westward across the western portion of the east
Pacific and into the central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch
NNNN

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Lala (CP2/CP012026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...LALA STRENGTHENING OVER THE CENTRAL PACIFIC... As of 5:00 PM HST Mon Aug 17 the center of Lala was located near 20.3, -165.5 with movement W at 12 mph. The minimum central pressure was 991 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 70 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Public Advisory Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Mon Aug 17 2026 
ZCZC HFOTCPCP2 ALL
TTAA00 PHFO DDHHMM
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  23
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM HST Mon Aug 17 2026
 
...LALA STRENGTHENING OVER THE CENTRAL PACIFIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 165.5W
ABOUT 255 MI...410 KM SSE OF FRENCH FRIGATE SHOALS
ABOUT 670 MI...1080 KM SE OF LISIANSKI ISLAND
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 265 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...991 MB...29.27 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument should
monitor the progress of Lala. Watches could be required for portions
of the area on Tuesday.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 165.5 West. Lala is 
moving toward the west near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this motion is 
expected to continue through Tuesday. A turn toward the 
west-northwest then northwest is forecast on Wednesday and Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 70 mph (110 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Strengthening is forecast during the next couple 
of days, and Lala is expected to become a hurricane again by 
Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 991 mb (29.27 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Pasch
 
NNNN

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Mon Aug 17 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 172041
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  22
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM HST Mon Aug 17 2026
 
Lala is a compact tropical storm. A large, curved convective band
wraps most of the way around the system in visible and infrared
satellite images. Objective UW-CIMSS D-MINT intensity estimates have
increased this morning based on recent SSMIS passive microwave data
that showed improved mid-level structure. In addition, HFO and JTWC
recently provided consensus T3.5 Dvorak intensity estimates. Based
on these data, the initial intensity is raised to 55 kt.
 
Lala is moving just south of due west (260/9 kt). A subtropical
ridge to the north of Lala will keep the storm on a westward heading
for the next 12-24 h. Then, a shortwave trough is forecast to move
over the northern Pacific and induce a weakness in the steering
ridge by midweek. This should cause Lala to turn northwestward and
then northward later this week. This forecast brings Lala toward
portions of the Papahanaumokuakea Marine National Monument on
Thursday and Thursday night, and watches may be required for parts
of that area on Tuesday. Track forecast confidence is higher than
yesterday since the track models are in better agreement on the
northward turn, though there is still some spread in how abrupt that
turn will be. Overall, the updated NHC forecast is slightly faster,
but otherwise very similar to the previous prediction.
 
The small size of Lala could make it prone to faster intensity
changes in either direction. The storm is currently moving within a
fairly dry mid-level environment and experiencing moderate westerly
shear. While these conditions are not ideal for strengthening, a
solidified inner core could allow Lala to resist some of these
inhibiting environmental factors and intensify over warm waters
(27-28 deg C). The hurricane regional models and Google Deep Mind
(GDMI) remain most aggressive with near-term strengthening. The NHC
intensity forecast has been adjusted upward slightly following the
simple consensus (IVCN) and shows Lala becoming a hurricane again by
late Tuesday. The longer-range forecast is tricky, as the global
models suggest some potential for positive trough interaction later
this week before strong southwesterly shear induces weakening. While
a secondary intensity peak is not shown in the official forecast,
some intensification in 3-4 days cannot be ruled out.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  17/2100Z 20.4N 164.3W   55 KT  65 MPH

 24H  18/1800Z 20.5N 167.6W   60 KT  70 MPH
